column2: Valmiki questions Narada about the ideal man, and Narada names Rama and recounts his exile, war, triumph, and righteous reign.
Valmiki curses a hunter for killing a loving kraunca, discovers grief shaped as shloka, and receives Brahmas command to compose Rama epic.
Valmiki meditates on Narada's tale and beholds Rama's whole life from birth through Lanka victory to homecoming and future deeds.
Valmiki teaches his Ramayana epic to Kusha and Lava, whose sweet singing before sages and Rama wins gifts and royal honor.
Dasharatha rules splendid Manu-built Ayodhya in rich Kosala on Sarayu, seat of Ikshvaku kings and coming Ramayana.
Dasharatha guards thriving Ayodhya where righteous well-fed citizens, dutiful varnas, and mighty horse elephant armies uphold dharma in plenty.
King Dasharatha rules the earth aided by eight virtuous ministers and priests Vasishtha and Vamadeva, keeping his peaceful realm just and prosperous.
Sonless Dasharatha plans a horse sacrifice, then Sumantra recounts Sanatkumara prophecy that sage Rishyashringa will grant him sons.
Lomapadas courtesans lure forest sage Rishyashringa to Anga with music and sweets, ending drought as rains greet his arrival.
Childless Dasharatha claims Rishyashringa and Shanta from joyful Lomapada, leads sage into decorated Ayodhya for heir-giving sacrifice
Dasaratha vows a horse sacrifice for sons, gains priestly promise of four mighty sons, and orders horse release and Sarayu ground preparation.
Dasharatha asks Vasishtha to stage an offspring rite, who orders lodgings, invites Janaka and all kings, and opens the sacrifice.
Dasharatha completes his flawless horse sacrifice with lavish feasts and gifts, then Rishyashringa promises him four lineage-bearing sons
Rishyashringa starts Dasharatha offspring rite as gods beg Brahma against cruel Ravana and seek Vishnu birth as four princes.
Vishnu agrees to kill Ravana as son of Dasharatha after a fire-born being delivers divine payasa for his three queens
Brahma orders gods to father shapeshifting monkey sons, who multiply into mighty hosts eager to kill Ravana and aid Rama.
Dasharatha celebrates the birth and naming of four princes, then honors arriving Vishvamitra and pledges to grant any wish.
Vishvamitra praises Dasharatha, demands ten-day loan of Rama to kill Maricha and Subahu defiling his rite, leaving king terrified.
Dasharatha refuses to give boy Rama to Vishvamitra, offers his own army instead, and learns Ravana sends Maricha and Subahu against the rite.
Angered by Dasharatha breaking his promise, Vishvamitra threatens departure while Vasishtha praises his weapons and urges sending Rama.
Dasharatha hands blessed Rama and Lakshmana to Vishvamitra, who leads them to Sarayu and teaches Rama hunger-banishing Bala and Atibala lore.
Vishvamitra wakes Rama and Lakshmana at dawn, leads them to the old ashram of Kama, tells how Shiva burned Kama bodiless, and lodges there overnight
Vishvamitra ferries Rama and Lakshmana across Ganga, explains roaring Sarayu meeting, recounts Tataka ravaging Malada and Karusha, and orders Rama to kill her.
Vishvamitra recounts Tataka boon-born might, Agastya curse and ravaging, then commands Rama to slay her for cows and brahmins.
Rama vows obedience to Vishvamitra, fells Tataka with a chest arrow, earns praise of gods and camps with Vishvamitra at dusk.
Pleased Vishvamitra bestows scores of divine weapons on Rama, who receives their mantras and commands the personified arms to attend him.
Rama learns weapon withdrawals from Vishvamitra, sends embodied weapons to await mental summons, and asks whose hermitage grove lies ahead.
Vishvamitra recounts how dwarf Vishnu reclaims three worlds from Bali and leads Rama to Siddhashrama to kill obstructing demons.
Rama sleeplessly guards Vishvamitra six-night rite, hurls Maricha a hundred yojanas into the ocean, slays Subahu and followers, and wins Siddhashrama honor.
Sages invite Rama and Lakshmana to Janaka sacrifice to see the unstringable divine bow and lead them from Siddhashrama to the Sona.
Vishvamitra traces Kusha sons founding four cities and tells how Vayu cripples Kushanabha hundred daughters after they refuse his marriage offer.
Kushanabha weds his hundred Vayu-crippled daughters to Brahmadatta, whose hand touch straightens them, then sends the joyful couples away.
Vishvamitra recounts his birth from Gadhi, his sister Satyavati becoming river Kaushiki, then halts at midnight and puts Rama to sleep.
Vishvamitra leads Rama to the Ganga bank and reveals her birth as Himavat's elder daughter, taken by gods, while Uma weds Rudra.
Vishvamitra tells Rama how alarmed gods halt Shiva after a century of union, and spilt brilliance births Kartikeya as Uma curses heaven barren.
Brahma directs gods to Agni and Ganga, whose cast embryo becomes gold and bears six-faced Skanda, whom gods anoint commander after Daitya victory.
Bhrigu grants childless Sagara a single heir through Keshini and sixty thousand sons through Sumati, but cruel Asamanja faces exile before Sagara plans sacrifice.
Vishvamitra tells Rama how Indra steals Sagara's horse, sending sixty thousand sons digging earth to Rasatala until gods appeal to Brahma.
Sagara sons honor four elephants bearing earth, confront Kapila over stolen horse, and perish as his wrathful humkara burns them to ashes.
Amshuman finds his fathers burnt to ashes, learns from Garuda only Ganga frees them, returns horse so Sagara completes sacrifice.
Bhagiratha wins Brahma's boon to bring Ganga for Sagara's sons after Amshuman and Dilipa die without freeing them.
Shiva bears sky-falling Ganga in his locks for years, then releases her toward Bindu lake where Bhagiratha leads her earthward.
Brahma declares Sagara's sixty thousand sons saved as Ganga floods their ashes, and Bhagiratha completes rites and rules joyfully.
Rama crosses Ganga to splendid Vishala and hears Vishvamitra tell how gods churn the ocean, win amrita, and destroy demons.
Diti wins Kashyapa boon for Indra-slaying son, but Indra serving her tapas splits her impure-sleeping womb sevenfold with his vajra.
Indra grants Diti Marut status for her forty-nine sons, then Vishvamitra traces Vishala kings to Sumati, who welcomes the travelers overnight.
Sumati honors Rama and Lakshmana overnight, then Vishvamitra shows Gautama's empty hermitage and tells how Gautama cursed Indra and Ahalya until Rama frees her.
Rama frees radiant Ahalya from Gautama curse as gods restore gelded Indra with ram testicles before Mithila journey.
Janaka welcomes Vishvamitra to his sacrifice, admires Rama and Lakshmana, and hears their lineage and journey from the sage.
Vishvamitra assures Shatananda that Ahalya reunites with Gautama, then Shatananda welcomes Rama and begins Vishvamitra's royal history.
Vasishtha welcomes Vishvamitra with worship and welfare talks, presses feast on his reluctant guest, then summons cow Shabala to feed the army.
Vasishtha feasts Vishvamitra's entire army through Shabala's magic, then firmly refuses to surrender her despite lavish elephants, horses and cows.
Shabala shakes off Vishvamitra's men, proves brahmin power beats Kshatriya, then spawns Pahlava and Shaka-Yavana hosts that destroy his army.
Shabala-born hosts destroy Vishvamitra's army, Vasishtha burns his hundred sons, and Shiva-armed Vishvamitra torches Vasishtha's hermitage in revenge.
Vasishtha swallows Vishvamitra's fiery arsenal and Brahmastra with his Brahma staff, humbling Vishvamitra into vowing tapas for brahmanhood.
Brahma names Vishvamitra rajarshi after fierce tapas, but dissatisfied Vishvamitra resumes austerities while rejected Trishanku begs Vasishtha sons for bodily heaven.
Vasishtha sons curse Trishanku into chandala form for defying them, and the outcast king begs Vishvamitra to send him bodily to heaven.
Vishvamitra shelters outcast Trishanku, summons sages for his bodily heaven rite, and curses scoffing Vasishthas to degraded dog-eating rebirths.
Vishvamitra hurls Trishanku bodily to heaven, halts his fall from Indra and wins him eternal headlong refuge among new southern stars.
Vishvamitra moves austerities to Pushkara while Ambarisha buys willing Shunahshepa as human victim after Indra steals his animal.
Vishvamitra curses disobedient sons and arms Shunahshepa with hymns that win long life from Indra at Ambarisha's sacrifice.
Menaka steals ten years from Vishvamitra's austerities until he dismisses her, wins Maharshi rank but resumes fiercer tapas for Brahmarshi.
Vishvamitra curses tempting Rambha to stand as stone for ten thousand years, then repents his anger and finds no peace.
Brahma grants Vishvamitra Brahmanhood after thousand-year silent tapas, Vasishtha befriends him and Janaka welcomes fulfilled sage.
Janaka recounts Shiva bow deposit, Sita furrow birth and failed suitors, then promises Sita to Rama if he strings the bow.
Rama lifts, strings and snaps Janaka's divine bow, and Janaka pledges Sita to him and sends ministers to fetch King Dasharatha.
Janaka's messengers invite Dasharatha to Mithila after Rama breaks the bow to wed Sita, and the delighted king orders march tomorrow.
Dasharatha leads his army, sages and treasure on a four-day march to Videha, where Janaka welcomes him and sets the wedding for dawn.
Janaka gathers Kushadhvaja and Dasharatha, then Vasishtha recites Solar lineage from Brahma to Rama and seeks daughters for Rama and Lakshmana.
Janaka recites his Nimi lineage, recalls slaying Sudhanva, offers Sita to Rama and Urmila to Lakshmana, and sets wedding day.
Vishvamitra seeks Kushadhvaja daughters for Bharata and Shatrughna, Janaka fixes four weddings while Dasaratha performs lavish cow gifts.
Janaka weds Sita to Rama, Urmila to Lakshmana, Mandavi to Bharata and Shrutakirti to Shatrughna amid celestial flowers and music.
Parashurama bars Dasaratha's homeward march, axe and bow blazing, while sages greet him and he hails Rama.
Parashurama ignores Dasaratha's plea and challenges Rama to string Vaishnava bow for duel, recounting Vishnu triumph over Shiva and bow descent through Richika.
Rama strings Parashurama bow, spares his life as brahmana, and looses the Vaishnava arrow to destroy his austerity-won worlds, sending humbled Parashurama to Mount Mahendra.
Rama gives his bow to Varuna, returns triumphant to Ayodhya with his bride, and lives happily serving his father with Sita.
Yudhajit escorts Bharata and Shatrughna to Kekaya while Rama wins Ayodhya through service, prompting Dasaratha to plan his consecration as crown prince.
Aged Dasaratha asks his assembly for rest and names Rama crown prince, and the rejoicing kings and citizens praise Rama and demand swift crowning.
Dasaratha orders Vasishtha and Vamadeva to ready Rama crowning, summons Rama, seats, embraces and counsels him, as Kausalya rewards messengers and citizens rejoice.
Dasaratha recalls Rama secretly, cites ill omens and Bharata absence, fixes tomorrow Pushya crowning with Sita fasting, and Rama tells Kausalya and Lakshmana.
Dasaratha sends Vasishtha to impose the night fast on Rama and Sita, and the priest finds Ayodhya streets thronged awaiting dawn crowning.
Rama and Sita fast overnight and worship Vishnu, while Ayodhya raises flags and lamps, praises Dasaratha, and crowds pour in for the crowning.
Manthara spots festival Ayodhya, learns Rama morrow crowning, warns sleeping Kaikeyi of ruin, but delighted Kaikeyi rewards her and welcomes Rama kingship.
Manthara discards the gift, warns Rama will ruin Bharata and enslave Kaikeyi to Kausalya, urging Bharata flight to forest and plotting for kingship.
Manthara reminds Kaikeyi of two war boons and sends her to the anger chamber to demand Bharata crowned and Rama exiled.
Dasaratha finds Kaikeyi fallen on bare ground, swears her any boon, then reels as she demands Bharata crowning and fourteen-year bark-clad Rama exile.
Dasharatha begs pitiless Kaikeyi to release her cruel boons, watches night pass in lamentation, then collapses senseless with grief
Kaikeyi threatens suicide to force truth-bound Dasharatha, who disowns her and Bharata before letting Kaikeyi summon Rama through Sumantra
Priests and ministers assemble consecration vessels and regalia, miss absent Dasharatha, while Sumantra hastens to Rama palace
Sumantra finds Rama enthroned beside Sita, delivers Dasharatha summons, and Rama races through cheering city toward palace with Lakshmana
Rama rides agaru-scented highway amid blessings and loyal vows, enters palace chambers, and leaves crowds awaiting his return
Kaikeyi demands Bharata crowned and Rama exiled fourteen years, and Rama accepts forest vow, consoles weeping Dasharatha, and departs
Rama passes priests and guards to find fasting Kaushalya worshipping Vishnu, tells her of fourteen-year exile, and watches her collapse lamenting
Lakshmana urges armed revolt and Kaushalya pleads filial duty, but Rama cites sages and ancestors, refuses disobedience, and begs leave
Rama tells Lakshmana to dismantle consecration gear without alarming Kaikeyi, blames fate alone, and urges calm withdrawal to forest
Lakshmana scorns fate, boasts his bow can guard Rama consecration against worlds, and Rama wipes his tears while holding to father word
Kausalya laments Rama's exile and begs to follow him, but Rama teaches duty to her living husband and Bharata's care, winning her consent and blessings.
Kausalya performs auspicious rites invoking all gods and seasons to protect forest-dwelling Rama, ties a mantra-guarded herb, embraces him, and sends him to Sita.
Rama finds Sita awaiting consecration, tells her of Kaikeyi's boons and his fourteen-year exile, and bids her serve his parents and honor Bharata.
Sita answers a wife shares her husband's fate, vows to tread thorns before him in the forest, and begs Rama to take her or die.
Rama tries to turn Sita back by describing the forest as hunger, leaf beds, bark clothes, roaring lions, snakes, insects, and tangled thorns.
Sita weeps that love turns forest faults to virtues, cites brahmanas foretelling exile, and threatens poison, fire, or water if Rama refuses her.
Sita reproaches Rama, vows thorns feel soft beside him, threatens poison if left, and Rama embraces her, grants leave, and bids her give wealth away.
Lakshmana vows to lead Rama with Sita through the forest and guard them, and Rama sends him to fetch arms and summon Suyajna for gifts.
Rama summons Suyajna and honors him with jewels, rewards teachers, servants, and dependents, and grants poor Trijata the cattle his hurled staff encircles.
Citizens lament Rama on foot with Sita and Lakshmana, vow to follow him leaving city a forest for Kaikeyi, while Rama seeks his father.
Rama seeks farewell from fainting Dasharatha before forest exile, refuses the offered throne and one-night delay, and yields the kingdom to Bharata.
Dasharatha orders army and riches to follow Rama, Kaikeyi invokes Sagara exiling Asamanja, Siddhartha refutes her, and Dasharatha vows to follow Rama.
Rama rejects royal retinue for bark garments, Kaikeyi shamelessly hands them out, Rama dresses helpless Sita, and commends Kausalya to Dasharatha.
Dasharatha faints at sage-clad Rama, orders chariot and jewels for Sita, Kausalya counsels wifely duty, and Rama takes leave of wailing mothers.
Rama, Sita and Lakshmana mount Sumantra chariot amid chasing citizens, Rama speeds past stumbling Dasharatha, and ministers halt the gazing king.
Palace queens wail for exiled protector Rama while fires die, planets menace, citizens despair, and bereft Ayodhya quakes.
Dasharatha gazes till Rama dust vanishes, renounces Kaikeyi and Bharata offerings, and stumbles into Kausalya house crying for Rama.
Grieving Kausalya calls triumphant Kaikeyi a freed snake, pictures exiles on forest roots, and dreams of showered homecoming.
Sumitra consoles wailing Kausalya that righteous Rama, served by Lakshmana and soothed by nature, will return to consecration.
Devoted citizens follow Rama chariot, Rama commends them to Bharata, brahmanas plead with Vajapeya umbrellas, and Tamasa bars the path.
Rama spends first night on Tamasa praising Bharata, lives on water only, and slips away at dawn while citizens lose his track.
Bereft citizens weep at home with closed markets, envy Lakshmana and forest pools, curse Kaikeyi, and lament like men facing death.
Rama drives deep through Kosala hearing villagers curse Dasharatha, crosses Vedashruti Gomati Syandika, and shows Manu-given land to Sita.
Rama halts by Ganga at Sringaverapura where friend Guha offers food and kingdom, Rama takes only water, and guards watch the night.
Wakeful Lakshmana tells Guha he cannot sleep while Rama lies on grass, Dasharatha will soon die, and widowed Ayodhya will perish.
Sumantra begs to follow into exile with chariot and fire, Rama sends him back with messages for all, and the exiles cross Ganga.
Rama grieves for helpless Dasharatha and Kausalya under Kaikeyi, bids Lakshmana guard his mother, and Lakshmana vows never to leave him.
Bharadvaja welcomes Rama Sita Lakshmana at Prayaga with cow and arghya, and sends them to dwell on holy Chitrakuta hill.
Bharadvaja guides the exiles over Yamuna by raft to Shyama banyan, then they kill deer and reach a river-bank dwelling.
Rama wakes Lakshmana hearing forest cries, shows Sita flowering woods and Chitrakuta peak, and Lakshmana builds their leaf hut.
Sumantra returns Rama-less to silent Ayodhya, tells crowds Rama sent him back at Ganga, and grieving Dasharatha faints as palace wails.
Revived Dasharatha questions Sumantra about forest life, hears Rama bows and bids Bharata honor mothers and king, Lakshmana condemns exile, and Sita weeps silent.
Sumantra pictures mourning forest and joyless Ayodhya, Dasharatha confesses hasty woman-driven exile, begs to see Rama, and faints lamenting.
Trembling Kausalya begs Sumantra to drive her to Dandaka, hears fearless Sita thrives clinging to Rama, yet wails still for her son.
Weeping Kausalya pictures delicate Sita suffering forest hardships, warns Rama will scorn Bharata-enjoyed kingdom, and grieving Dasharatha faints.
Rebuked Dasharatha recalls past misdeed, begs Kausalya pardon, hears grief destroys all and nights seem years, then sinks grieving to sleep.
Sleepless Dasharatha recalls youthful sound-shot sin, mistaking water pot for elephant on Sarayu and mortally wounding a parent-serving ascetic.
Dasharatha tells blind parents of mistaken killing, leads them to corpse, hears radiant son ascend, and receives curse to die of son grief.
Dawn attendants find Dasharatha lifeless, bedchamber women wail like leaderless elephants, and awakened Kausalya Sumitra fall crying as palace mourns.
Kausalya curses fulfilled Kaikeyi and pictures frightened Sita, ministers lay Dasharatha in oil awaiting sons, and Ayodhya censures Bharata mother.
Brahmana ministers urge Vasishtha to crown a prince at once, warning kingless Ayodhya faces rain failure, lawlessness, and ruin after Dasharatha death and Rama exile.
Vasishtha orders swift messengers to fetch Bharata from Rajagriha at once, concealing Dasharatha death and Rama exile with urgent summons.
Bharata suffers a dreadful night dream of his soiled father falling, oil drinking, and dark omens foretelling death for Rama, Lakshmana, or king.
Bharata questions secretive messengers about his family welfare, takes leave of his grandfather, and hastens homeward with Shatrughna and rich gifts.
Bharata races homeward across rivers and forests for seven nights, then finds silent dusty Ayodhya emptied of joy and full of evil omens.
Kaikeyi tells Bharata his father is dead and Rama exiled to Dandaka by her demand, urging him to cremate the king and seize the throne.
Bharata denounces Kaikeyi as his family death-night, rejects her stolen kingdom, and vows to bring beloved Rama back from the forest.
Bharata curses cruel Kaikeyi to hell as demoness, cites grieving cow Surabhi, and vows to bring Rama back before entering forest himself.
Kausalya bitterly charges Bharata with winning a thornless throne by exile, then Bharata swears dreadful oaths denying any part in Rama banishment.
Vasishtha steadies grieving Bharata, priests bear oil-preserved Dasharatha on a bier, cremate him with chants, and all offer Sarayu water for ten days.
Bharata performs shraddha gifts, laments at ash-covered pyre with Shatrughna, then Vasishtha and Sumantra console grieving brothers toward remaining rites.
Shatrughna seizes adorned Manthara, drags her wailing across palace and reviles Kaikeyi, until Bharata forbids killing women and frees her.
Ministers offer leaderless throne to Bharata, who refuses for elder Rama, vows forest dwelling, and orders a leveled road to fetch his brother.
Workmen clear forests, level pits, plant trees, dig tanks and wells, then raise moated bannered camps as the adorned highway reaches the Ganga.
Bards wake grieving Bharata who disclaims kingship and mourns rudderless Lakshmi, then Vasishtha convenes the golden assembly as subjects hail him like Dasharatha.
Vasishtha urges Bharata to take the thornless kingdom, but tearful Bharata declares Rama alone king, disowns mother sin, and musters the army to fetch him.
Bharata leads elephants chariots horses, mothers citizens artisans and brahmanas to the Ganga, camps the glad army, and offers river water for his father.
Guha sights the oceanlike army, rallies fishermen guards suspecting attack on Rama, then brings fish meat honey and offers lodging after Sumantra introduces him.
Bharata asks Guha the forest path, swears he comes only to fetch fatherlike Rama, and Guha praises his renunciation as night grief burns him sleepless.
Guha tells how sleepless Lakshmana refuses a bed and foretells widowed earth, then ferries the exiles across the Ganga at dawn.
Bharata faints at Guha tidings, then learns Rama fasted on water and slept on grass while Lakshmana stood guard all night.
Bharata mourns Rama grass bed under the ingudi tree, recalls palace luxury on bare earth, and vows ground sleep on roots.
Bharata summons Guha at dawn, ferries mothers priests and army across the Ganga in five hundred boats, then marches toward Prayaga forest.
Bharata leaves his army behind, enters Bharadvaja ashram on foot with Vasishtha, denies craving Rama kingdom, and learns Rama dwells at Chitrakuta.
Bharadvaja magically feasts Bharata entire army with Vishvakarman palaces, payasa rivers, Gandharva music, and sixty thousand women.
Bharata learns the Chitrakuta road from Bharadvaja, presents his mothers, denounces Kaikeyi, hears Rama exile brings good, and marches south.
Bharata halts his dusty fourfold army before flowered Chitrakuta, finds smoke in the forest, and advances with Sumantra and his preceptor toward it.
Rama comforts Sita by praising mineral peaked Chitrakuta, flowering trees, kinnara lovers, waterfalls, and forest life repaying father debt and pleasing Bharata.
Rama shows Sita the lotus Mandakini with bathing sages, dancing trees, and drinking herds, urging her to treat hill as Ayodhya and river as Sarayu.
Lakshmana climbs a sala tree, mistakes Bharata army for attack, arms for battle hiding Sita, and vows to kill Bharata avenging exile.
Rama calms Lakshmana's fury toward Bharata's approaching army, trusts Bharata's goodwill, and watches his great army camp peacefully by Chitrakuta.
Bharata stations his army, vows no peace until he sees Rama, and joyfully finds his hermitage smoke rising over Chitrakuta.
Bharata finds Rama's leaf hut in Chitrakuta, laments his fallen splendor, and falls speechless and weeping at his brother's feet.
Rama embraces Bharata and questions him at length about Dasharatha, the queens, ministers, spies, treasury, army, and Ayodhya's welfare.
Bharata announces Dasharatha's death, and shattered Rama faints, then offers water and ingudi cakes to his father at the Mandakini.
The queens reach Chitrakuta, grieve over Rama's forest fare and fallen splendor, and Rama honors his mothers and Vasishtha before all.
Bharata begs Rama to accept the kingdom after Dasharatha's death, but Rama refuses and bids him rule Ayodhya while he keeps their father's fourteen-year command.
Bharata again offers Rama the kingdom with parables, Rama preaches impermanence and obedience to Dasharatha, and Bharata threatens to follow him into exile.
Rama recalls Dasharatha's promised boons to Kaikeyi, upholds his fourteen-year exile, and sends Bharata back to rule Ayodhya and save their father.
Jabali urges Rama to abandon ancestral duty as meaningless, deny the afterlife, and accept Bharata's offered throne in prosperous Ayodhya.
Rama refutes Jabali claim that wrong can look right, praising truth as dharma root and vowing to keep father forest promise.
Vasishtha calms angry Rama, traces Solar line from Brahma to Dasaratha, and bids eldest Rama rule jewelled earth.
Rama honors parents debt and father command, refuses Bharata fasting vow, and Bharata offers forest exile instead.
Seers praise Rama Bharata meeting, Bharata begs for rule, and Rama gives gold sandals and dismissal.
Bharata bears Rama sandals past Bharadvaja counsel, crosses Yamuna Ganga, and mourns ruined Ayodhya from afar.
Bharata enters dark silent Ayodhya in similes of eclipsed night and dry river, and asks why music has ceased.
Bharata leaves mothers in Ayodhya, crowns Rama sandals at Nandigrama, and rules as bark clad ascetic awaiting return.
Rama marks eager whispering ascetics, learns Khara demons befoul rites, and watches Kulapati abandon Chitrakuta ashram.
Rama quits trampled Chitrakuta for Atri hermitage, where Atri praises Anasuya drought Ganga tapas and Sita seeks her wifely teaching.
Sita affirms husband devotion with Savitri example, receives Anasuya divine dress and unguent, then recounts furrow birth, bow breaking, and wedding.
Anasuya sends adorned Sita to Rama at dusk, Rama rejoices in her gifts, and ascetics guide the trio into demon beset forest.
Rama enters Dandakaranya and awed sages lodge him as guest, then remind him kings taking revenue must protect forest ascetics.
Man-eating Viradha seizes Sita and claims her as wife, Rama despairs over Kaikeyi's wish fulfilled, and Lakshmana vows to kill the rakshasa.
Rama shatters Viradha's spear and arms, the fallen rakshasa reveals cursed gandharva Tumburu freed by Rama, and brothers bury him heaven-bound.
Rama watches Indra court Sharabhanga to Brahmaloka, the sage refuses to go unseen by Rama, then enters fire and rises radiant to Brahma.
Forest ascetics show Rama slaughtered sages and beg refuge from rakshasas, and Rama vows battle-slaughter then marches toward Sutikshna.
Rama reaches Sutikshna's secluded ashram, the sage offers tapas-won worlds and lodging, but Rama declines a long stay lest his bow disturb fearless deer.
After dawn worship Rama takes leave of embracing Sutikshna, tours the Dandaka hermitage circle, and Sita hands the brothers bows, quivers, and swords.
Sita warns Rama that bearing arms may breed causeless cruelty, telling how a sword-guarding ascetic turned ruthless and fell to hell.
Rama answers Sita that devoured sages sought his refuge, he pledged their protection, and truth outweighs life, Sita, and Lakshmana.
Rama hears Mandakarni's lake marvel, sojourns ten years among hermitages, learns Agastya's road with the Vatapi tale, and reaches Agastya's dread-rakshasa-free grove.
Lakshmana announces Rama party to Agastya disciple, and delighted Agastya welcomes them, worships, feasts, and gifts Vishnu bow, arrow, quivers, and sword.
Pleased Agastya comforts travel-weary Rama party, praises faithful Sita, and directs Rama to settle happily at forested Panchavati near Godavari.
En route Rama meets vulture Jatayu, hears his vast creation genealogy and Aruna birth, embraces father friend, and gains Sita guardian for Panchavati.
At Panchavati Rama selects a flowering Godavari site, Lakshmana quickly builds a leaf hut and worships, and Rama rejoices and dwells happily.
At dawn by Godavari Lakshmana depicts frosty hemanta and ascetic Bharata, blames Kaikeyi, while Rama forbids censure and bathes worshipping sun.
Shurpanakha lusts for handsome Rama at his hut, hears his exile tale, names her demon brothers, and demands marriage while threatening to eat Sita.
Rama and Lakshmana jestingly deflect lusting Shurpanakha, who rushes to eat Sita, so Rama orders and Lakshmana cuts her ears and nose.
Mutilated Shurpanakha describes two youths and Sita to furious Khara, demands their blood, and Khara dispatches fourteen demons to kill them.
Fourteen demons threaten lone Rama at his hut, but Rama shatters their pikes and fells them all with blazing arrows as Shurpanakha wails.
Shurpanakha reports Rama slaughtered fourteen heroes, begs Khara to kill him threatening suicide, and taunts Khara cannot face Rama brilliance.
Stung by Shurpanakha, Khara musters fourteen thousand demons, mounts his ornate war chariot, and marches roaring from Janasthana against Rama.
As Khara marches, dread omens rain blood and darkness, but boasting Khara scorns them and leads his doomed host toward Rama.
Reading dire omens, Rama sends Lakshmana and Sita to a mountain cave, dons armor, and blazes alone against fourteen thousand demons.
Showered with missiles by thousands, unshaken Rama answers with countless arrows, shredding bows and bodies until survivors flee to Khara.
Rama severs Dushana arms and club, beheads three rushing chiefs, and annihilates fourteen thousand demons, leaving only Khara and Trishiras.
Trishiras wins leave to face Rama alone, wounds his forehead, but Rama fells horses, driver, banner, and three heads.
Khara and Rama duel arrow for arrow until Rama shatters banner, horses, chariot, and bow, leaving Khara chariotless and bowless on foot.
Righteous Rama lectures chariotless Khara on reaping evil, scornful Khara answers with boasts, then hurls a mace Rama shatters midair.
Rama mocks mace-less Khara, fells him with Indra-given arrow, and honored by sages rejoins Sita and Lakshmana at the ashram.
Seeing fourteen thousand slain, Shurpanakha flees to Lanka and finds mighty ten-necked Ravana enthroned, scarred, and dreaded by gods.
Distressed Shurpanakha scolds pleasure-blind Ravana before ministers, reports Rama alone slew fourteen thousand rakshasas, and Ravana ponders long.
Questioned by Ravana, Shurpanakha describes irresistible Rama, devoted Lakshmana, and matchless Sita, urging him to kill the brothers and seize Sita.
Ravana resolves alone, drives his jewelled wish-going chariot to the ocean shore, views sages towns and Garuda's Subhadra banyan, and reaches Maricha's hermitage.
Ravana tells Maricha Rama wiped out Janasthana's fourteen thousand, vilifies Rama as cruel exile, and demands he lure Sita as a golden deer for abduction.
Maricha warns Ravana Rama is Mahendra-like dharma embodied, predicts Sita will doom Lanka, and urges counsel with Vibhishana-led ministers.
Maricha recalls Vishvamitra fetching boy Rama, scorning the child, rushing the altar, and being hurled a hundred leagues into ocean by one arrow.
Maricha recalls returning as a man-eating horned deer, surviving Rama's three arrows while companions died, and now seeing Rama in every tree.
Ravana rejects Maricha's wholesome counsel as barren seed, asserts kings bear five divine forms, and threatens death unless he lures Sita as golden deer.
Maricha asks what foe advised ruin, warns sharp kings destroy subjects like jackals sheep, and foretells all rakshasas dead if Sita comes.
Yielding to fear, Maricha boards Ravana's mule-drawn chariot to Dandaka, becomes a jewelled golden deer, and amazed flower-picking Sita gazes fondly.
Sita begs Rama to fetch a jeweled golden deer, and despite Lakshmana warning it is Maricha trickery, Rama vows to kill or capture it.
Rama chases elusive golden deer into forest, kills Maricha with Brahma weapon, then hearing his Rama-voiced cry fears for Sita and rushes back.
Sita mistakes Maricha cry for Rama and orders Lakshmana to help, then reviles his refusal as lust until shamed Lakshmana leaves her to forest gods.
Lakshmana gone, Ravana approaches lonely Sita disguised as a mendicant and praises her beauty, while Sita honors him with seat water and forest food.
Questioned by her mendicant guest, Sita recounts her Ayodhya exile, then rejects Ravana self-revealed suitor with lion jackal warnings and steadfast devotion to Rama.
Ravana boasts he humbled Kubera seized Pushpaka and rules golden Lanka, dismissing Rama as dethroned mortal, but furious Sita warns stealing his wife means death.
Enraged Ravana sheds mendicant disguise for ten-faced terror, seizes screaming Sita onto his chariot, while she begs trees rivers and gods to tell Rama.
Wakeful Jatayu blocks Ravana skyward flight, declares Sita Rama inviolable queen, lectures him on kingly dharma, and though aged offers mortal battle.
Ravana and Jatayu clash fiercely overhead, and though arrows wound the eagle, Jatayu wrecks bow chariot mules with claws before Ravana cuts off his wings.
Sword-maimed Jatayu collapses bleeding while Ravana drags lamenting Sita by hair skyward as worlds darken, flowers jewels rain down, and nature mourns.
Captive Sita rebukes flying Ravana as cowardly thief and warns Rama will kill him, but wailing helplessly stays in his grasp.
Flying Sita drops her scarf and jewels among five monkeys as message, while Ravana carries her across ocean into Lanka.
Ravana shows Sita his jeweled palace and pleasures, boasts Lanka impregnable, and begs her to become his chief wife.
Sita puts straw between herself and Ravana, defies him with Rama's vengeance, and is confined weeping in Ashokavana.
Rama slays disguised Maricha, hears an evil jackal howl, meets Lakshmana coming without Sita, and fears demons seized her.
Rama grieves Sita's absence, questions Lakshmana desperately, blames demons avenging Khara, and returns to find shelter empty.
Lakshmana explains Sita's harsh insults drove him from her side, and Rama condemns abandoning her to demons.
Rama finds the hut empty and strewn, laments Sita stolen or eaten, and begs trees and beasts to reveal her.
Rama wails with uplifted arms before the wrecked hermitage while Lakshmana urges search, yet together they find no Sita.
Rama questions silent Godavari, finds Sita's flowers and battle wreckage, and vows to destroy worlds unless gods return her.
Lakshmana calms world-burning Rama grieving Sita, reads lone battle marks, and urges searching with sages before righteous war.
Lakshmana consoles grieving Rama with mortal fate examples and urges him to seek the foe instead of burning worlds.
Rama mistakes fallen Jatayu for Sitas eater, then embraces the dying bird as it names Ravana and tells of its failed rescue.
Dying Jatayu names Ravana as Vishravas son bound south, then Rama cremates him, offers meat and water, and wins him heaven.
Seeking Sita westward past Janasthana, Rama and Lakshmana meet monstrous belly-mouthed Kabandha and fall seized in his yojana arms.
Seized by Kabandha, Rama and Lakshmana sever his arms, declare their Sita quest, and hear his welcome and promised tale.
Spared Kabandha tells his sage curse and Indra maiming, seeks fire release, and promises a friend who knows the thief.
Burnt Kabandha rises radiant in a swan car and bids Rama befriend exiled Sugriva, who can find Sita worldwide.
Skyborne Kabandha maps the westward road to lotus Pampa, deathless flowers, Shabari, and Sugrivas Rishyamuka refuge.
Rama and Lakshmana reach Shabaris ashram, hear her sages foretold their coming, and grant her fire ascent to heaven.
After Shabaris ascent, Rama and Lakshmana reach flowering Pampa, mourn in love, and turn toward Sugrivas Rishyamuka hill.
Rama mourns stolen Sita beside spring-blooming Pampa and advances with Lakshmana toward monkey-guarded Rishyamuka.
Sugriva mistakes armed Rama and Lakshmana for Vali agents, flees the hill, and sends Hanuman to learn their intent.
Hanuman meets Rama and Lakshmana as a mendicant, praises their splendor, and offers Sugriva friendship while Rama rejoices.
Lakshmana tells Hanuman of Rama exile and Sita theft, and Hanuman promises Sugriva help and leads them to him.
Hanuman presents Rama to Sugriva on Malaya, and the two clasp hands and circle fire-sealed friendship.
Sugriva promises to restore Sita, shows the garments she dropped when Ravana bore her wailing overhead, and Rama weeps.
Sugriva vows to kill Ravana and counsels steadfast Rama to quit grief, and Rama pledges truth and seeks Sita.
Sugriva tells of Vali robbing his wife and kingdom, and Rama vows his arrows will fell brother-abusing Vali.
Sugriva tells how he guarded a cave for Vali, mistook blood for his death, accepted the crown, and earned exile.
Sugriva tells how returning Vali scorned his pleas, stripped and banished him, and Rama vows unfailing shafts.
Sugriva recounts Vali's leap, Dundubhi slaying and Matanga curse, shows bones and salas, then doubts Rama after toe-flicking corpse ten yojanas.
Rama pierces seven salas with one arrow, heartens doubting Sugriva, withholds his shot from twin brothers, and Lakshmana garlands Sugriva for rematch.
Rama marches toward Kishkindha with Sugriva and monkey chiefs, pauses to honor the unassailable Saptajana grove, then sights Vali-guarded Kishkindha.
Rama steadies roaring Sugriva near hidden Kishkindha, promises one arrow will fell Vali, and sends garland-marked Sugriva to draw his brother out.
Furious Vali rushes at Sugriva's earth-shaking challenge, but Tara clings to him, warns of Rama-backed strength, and begs peace and Sugriva crowning.
Vali spurns Tara's plea, battles Sugriva with fist and sala, then falls senseless when Rama plants a venomous arrow in his chest.
Vali, splendid in Indra's garland, accuses hidden Rama of unrighteous back-shooting, offers to bind Ravana and fetch Sita, then falls silent.
Rama justifies shooting Vali for seizing brother Sugriva's wife Ruma under Bharata's law, and dying Vali accepts, entrusting Angada and Tara to him.
Vali lies speechless near death while Tara rushes past fleeing monkeys, rejects crowning Angada, and collapses wailing upon her husband as Sugriva grieves.
Tara embraces slain Vali, mourns lost dalliance and widowhood, commends Angada to him, bids Sugriva enjoy Ruma and kingdom, then resolves to starve beside him.
Hanuman consoles fallen Tara with karma teaching and urges crowning Angada, but Tara refuses rule and chooses death beside Vali.
Dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada and Tara counsel, surrenders golden garland, advises Angada obedience, then dies as Tara collapses.
Tara kisses dead Vali and laments widowhood, shows Angada to his father, watches Nila draw the arrow, then mourns her ruined life.
Rama preaches fate and urges next rites, Lakshmana orders Vali cremation with bier and stores, then Sugriva cremates Vali with wailing kin and offers water.
Hanuman invites Rama to enter Kishkindha, Rama refuses exile vow, crowns Sugriva and Angada heir amid Vedic anointing and festivity.
Rama grieves sleepless for Sita on Prasravana hill, Lakshmana rouses his sleeping valor, and Rama resolves awaiting autumn to destroy Ravana.
Rama describes rainy season clouds, birds and rivers to Lakshmana, contrasts reveling Sugriva with his own sinking grief, then resolves awaiting time.
Hanuman finds Sugriva sporting with Tara and neglecting Rama, urges timely Sita search, then Sugriva orders Nila to muster armies within fifteen nights.
Autumn moonlit Rama faints recalling lost Sita and idle Sugriva, Lakshmana consoles him, then Rama threatens faithless Sugriva with Vali path unless he acts.
Lakshmana vows killing false Sugriva and crowning Angada, Rama restrains him to gentle warning, then Lakshmana storms armed into monkey-filled Kishkindha.
Sugriva rises alarmed at angry Lakshmana, consults ministers, then heeds Hanuman recalling Rama slaying Vali, autumn arrival, his negligence, and urging folded-hand apology and obedience.
Lakshmana enters jewelled Kishkindha past guards and chiefs houses, crosses seven enclosures amid music and women, and finds Sugriva enthroned with Ruma.
Lakshmana rebukes pleasure-bound Sugriva clasping Ruma, brands promise-breaking ingratitude toward Rama as unexpiable, and warns him against following Vali path.
Tara soothes blazing Lakshmana, defends grateful Sugriva blessed by Rama, pleads indulgence like Vishvamitra, cites countless Lanka foes, and promises arriving hosts.
Lakshmana accepts Tara humble plea, Sugriva sheds fear, owns Rama-restored glory, vows to follow against Ravana, and wins Lakshmana praise and summons to Rama.
Sugriva orders Hanuman to summon monkeys from five peaks and all quarters in ten days on pain of death, and crores arrive with tribute.
Lakshmana leads Sugriva from Kishkindha by palanquin to Rama, who preaches timely dharma and enterprise, while Sugriva reports gathering hosts soon to fetch Sita.
Rama embraces Sugriva, vows soon to kill Ravana, then hails the dust-raising arrival of Shatabali, Sushena, Kesari, Gavaksha, Angada, Hanuman and countless hosts.
Sugriva offers his stationed army to Rama, who seeks living Sita and Ravana lair, sending Vinata with a hundred thousand east to Udaya.
Sugriva sends Angada-led Nila, Hanuman and Jambavan south through Vindhya, Godavari, Malaya, Kaveri, Mahendra and ocean isles, promising fortune to first finder.
Sugriva dispatches Sushena with a hundred thousand monkeys westward through rich lands, seas, golden peaks, and Meru to find Sita within a month.
Sugriva sends Shatabali with a hundred thousand monkeys north through Himalayan tribes, Kubera realms, Uttara Kurus, and Somagiri to find Sita.
Sugriva entrusts Hanuman alone for his unmatched speed and strength, and Rama gives his named ring as token for Sita.
Monkey hosts scatter to all quarters boasting they will fetch Sita and kill Ravana, while Rama waits at Prasravana for the set month.
Rama asks how Sugriva knows the whole earth, and Sugriva recounts fleeing vengeful Vali across all quarters to refuge at Rishyamuka.
East, north, and west hosts return empty-handed after a month, reporting searched lands and slain beasts, leaving hope in southbound Hanuman.
Hanuman, Angada, and Tara comb Vindhya caves and cursed Kandu forest, where Angada fells a charging asura, yet find neither Sita nor Ravana.
Angada rallies despairing monkeys to persevere under Sugriva and Rama fear, leading them again over Vindhya peaks and forests without finding Sita.
Parched southern monkeys enter a dark bird-marked cave for water and emerge into a golden forest of lotus ponds, mansions, and a blazing ascetic woman.
Hanuman questions the fasting ascetic, who credits Maya magic, Indra slaying him, Brahma granting woods to Hema, then offers food.
Hanuman tells ascetic Swayamprabha of Rama exile, Sita abduction, southern search and cave entry, pleasing her though she wants nothing.
Swayamprabha frees monkeys from the cave, and facing an expired deadline Angada vows a seashore fast while Tara urges hiding.
Hanuman splits Angada followers, warns Lakshmana arrows will shatter cave refuge, and urges return to forgiving Sugriva for kingship.
Angada denounces faithless Sugriva as brother-betrayer, bids farewell to family, and fasts with weeping monkeys on the seashore.
Long-lived Sampati threatens to eat fasting monkeys, and Angada lament recalls Jatayu death for Sita, startling his grieving brother.
Angada answers meat-fearing vulture Sampati, recounts Rama alliance, Jatayu funeral, Vali slaying, and southern search missing deadline.
Wingless Sampati recalls sun-scorched fall, reports seeing Ravana bear Sita to sea-girt Lanka a hundred yojanas south, and seeks ocean water for Jatayu.
Questioned by Jambavan, Sampati recounts son Suparshva sighting Ravana bear wailing Sita at Mahendra, and urges swift resolve despite wingless age.
Bathed Sampati bids silent monkeys hear truth, recalls six-night swoon, Vindhya recognition, and sage Nishakara fragrant ashram.
Sampati confesses prideful sun wager with Jatayu, shielding his brother while burning his own wings, and falling kinless on Vindhya longing for death.
Sage Nishakara foretells Rama exile, Sita abduction, and Indra food, charging wingless Sampati to await Rama monkey messengers.
Sampati regains burnt wings as he speaks, rejoices in restored youth, and sends the heartened monkeys onward to seek Sita.
Angada leads the monkeys to the vast sea, rebukes their despair, and challenges any hero to leap a hundred yojanas.
Chiefs declare leaps from ten to ninety yojanas, Angada offers a hundred without sure return, and Jambavan forbids risking their leader.
Jambavan reminds silent Hanuman of his divine birth, childhood leap at the sun, and god-given boons, urging him to leap the ocean.
Hanuman swells with power, boasts his sky-crossing feats, climbs Mount Mahendra, and hurls his mind toward Lanka as the peak trembles.
Hanuman leaps the hundred-yojana ocean past Mainaka, Surasa, and Simhika and lands shrunken to find Sita.
Hanuman surveys guarded Lanka from Trikuta, judges war hopeless, and shrinks cat-small to enter unseen at dusk.
Hanuman slips through lamp-lit Lanka past its huge deformed guard and enters Ravana palace heartened by Rama prowess.
Hanuman searches moonlit Lanka homes among drunken couples and starlike wives but never finds Sita.
Hanuman searches house after house of Prahasta, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana, Indrajit, and lesser chiefs, then reenters Ravana palace.
Hanuman marvels at Ravana peerless Pushpaka vimana with jewel lattices and crafted beasts but misses Janaki.
Hanuman climbs Pushpaka to Ravana jewelled hall, sees a thousand tangled sleeping wives, and judges Sita beyond them all.
Hanuman studies sleeping Ravana scarred arms and jewelled wives, mistakes radiant Mandodari for Sita, and frolics.
Hanuman concludes Sita would shun revelry, scours Ravana drink hall past meats wines and sleepers, yet finds no Janaki.
Hanuman misses Sita after combing palace, fears death and Sugriva wrath, then vows tireless renewed search.
Hanuman searches Lanka in vain for Sita, pictures Rama and kin dying if he reports failure, and resolves to search Ashokavana again.
Hanuman enters flowering Ashokavana, climbs a golden shimshapa, and waits hidden for grieving Sita at twilight river.
Hanuman spots captive Sita beneath a palace tower, matches her ornaments and sari to Rama account, and praises Rama delighted.
Hanuman reflects that Rama slew Vali, Kabandha and Janasthana hosts for Sita, deems worlds worthless beside her, and hides convinced.
Under moonlight Hanuman studies Sita guarded by grotesque meat-eating rakshasis and rejoices, weeping and bowing to Rama.
Ravana wakes brooding on Sita, enters Ashokavana flaunting jewels with a hundred wives, and approaches her while Hanuman watches hidden.
Trembling Sita cowers from adorned Ravana on bare ground amid eclipse-like similes, praying palms-joined for his defeat as he tempts her.
Ravana woos Sita with queenship, jewels and pleasures, boasts matchless might, and mocks exiled Rama as fallen beyond rescue.
Straw-guarded Sita rebukes Ravana, vows oneness with Rama, and warns Rama arrows leave him no refuge.
Ravana grants Sita two months to yield, threatens kitchen death, commands rakshasis to break her, then leaves seduced by Dhanyamalini.
Ravana leaves Sita to guards, and rakshasis urge her to marry him, praising his lineage, victories, wealth, and threatening death for refusal.
Sita rejects the guards who demand she abandon Rama for Ravana, and Vinata, Vikata, Chandodari, Praghasa, Ajamukhi, and Shurpanakha threaten to devour her.
Threatened and alone, Sita clings to a flowering ashoka bough, wails for Rama, Lakshmana, and her mothers, and curses helpless captivity.
Sita vows she will never touch Ravana, recalls Rama slaying fourteen thousand demons and Viradha, and foretells burning Lanka despite despairing rescue.
Aged Trijata stops the guards from eating Sita and recounts a terrible dream of Rama triumphant, Ravana fallen southward, and Lanka drowned.
Convinced that Rama ignores her or lies dead, Sita seizes her braid as a noose for hanging, then saving omens suddenly appear.
As Sita grieves, her left eye, arm, and thigh throb auspiciously, her garment slips, and her moonlike face shines freed from sorrow.
Hidden in the tree, Hanuman hears everything and debates consoling Sita, fearing speech will betray him yet silence will kill her.
From the branches Hanuman sweetly recounts Dasaratha glory, Rama forest exile with wife and brother, Ravana abduction, and his finding Sita.
Seeing the humble talking monkey, Sita faints for a dream, revives sleepless, reasons grief conjures visions, and prays his words prove true.
Hanuman questions grieving Sita beneath her tree, hears her embrace exile and abduction, and learns Ravana grants her only two months to live.
Hanuman declares himself Rama messenger with greetings, endures Sita fearing Ravana trick, and proves himself by praising Rama and naming his leap.
Pressed for proof, Hanuman describes Rama marks, recounts Sugriva alliance and Valin death, and traces Sampati clue and ocean leap to Sita.
Hanuman shows Rama inscribed ring to convince Sita, who praises his leap and anxiously asks after Rama, Lakshmana, and rescue.
Sita warns her year ends in two months, refuses Hanuman back ride lest Rama lose glory, and demands Rama himself kill Ravana and fetch her.
Hanuman approves her refusal, seeks a token, hears the crow and Brahma shaft tale, receives her crest jewel, and turns homeward glad.
Sita charges Hanuman with welfare messages and urges saving valor, doubts monkeys can cross the sea, and hears Sugriva host will leap and burn foes.
Sita adds crow reed and lost tilaka tokens, sets one month of life, and tearfully speeds Hanuman north with pleas for rescue.
Duty done but battle untested, Hanuman scorns conciliation, gift, and division, wrecks the pleasure grove, and waits at the arch for Ravana force.
Rakshasis report the wrecked grove and talking monkey, Ravana sends eighty thousand Kinkaras, and Hanuman slays them with an iron bar.
Hanuman smashes the shrine hall, proclaims Rama victory, slays a hundred shrine guards with a pillar, and warns Lanka of Sugriva invasion.
Jambumali wounds Hanuman with sharp arrows, Hanuman shatters rock and tree missiles, then crushes mighty Jambumali with a whirled beam.
Seven minister sons shower Hanuman with arrows, Hanuman dodges in the sky, then crushes them with fists feet and roar.
Ravana warns five generals against a mighty monkey being, Hanuman kills Virupaksha Yupaksha Durdhara Praghasa Bhasakarna and destroys their army.
Prince Aksha wounds Hanuman in fierce sky battle, Hanuman hesitates at his valor, then smashes his chariot and dashes him to death.
Indrajit duels Hanuman to stalemate, binds him with the Brahma weapon, and drags the willing captive before Ravana for questioning.
Bound Hanuman gazes at jewel crowned ten headed Ravana enthroned with women and ministers, and marvels at his splendor and menace.
Prahasta asks if Hanuman serves gods or Vishnu, Hanuman owns his monkey birth, admits wrecking the grove, and claims Rama embassy.
Hanuman recounts Rama exile Sugriva alliance and ocean leap, warns Sita spells Lanka ruin, and Ravana answers by ordering his death.
Ravana orders the envoy killed, Vibhishana condemns messenger killing, lists lawful punishments, and urges battle with Rama instead.
Ravana spares Hanuman death at Vibhishana urging, burns his tail for parade, but Sita prayer cools fire as Hanuman breaks free.
Hanuman torches Lanka palaces with his burning tail, wind fans citywide fire, and he quenches his tail in the ocean.
Hanuman fears Sita burned with Lanka, laments his anger, then hears bards confirm her safety and rejoices.
Hanuman reassures Sita Rama comes with armies, climbs Mount Arishta, and leaps north crushing the peak earthward.
Hanuman flies cloud-wreathed over the ocean, roars to waiting monkeys, and announces Sita found in Ashoka grove.
Hanuman recounts ocean ordeals, Sita discovery, Ravana threats, envoy plea, tail fire, Lanka burning, and completed mission.
Hanuman praises chaste Sita power to burn worlds, describes her fasting guard-bound grief, and urges swift rescue.
Angada urges fetching Sita now and boasts monkeys can crush Lanka, but Jambavan defers to Rama judgment.
Monkeys accept Jambavan counsel, leap to Sugriva Madhuvana, and revel drunkenly beating its keeper Dadhimukha.
Angada sanctions honey feasting, monkeys batter guards, and mauled Dadhimukha flies to complain at Sugriva feet.
Dadhimukha reports ravaged Madhuvana and beaten guards, Sugriva declares Sita found through Hanuman, forgives the monkeys and craves their tidings.
Dadhimukha carries Sugriva pardon to Madhuvana, Angada leads leaping host to Kishkindha, and Hanuman bows reporting Sita alive to Rama.
Angada-led host bows on Prasravana, Hanuman reports leaping the ocean, finding Sita in Ravana palace, winning trust, and bringing her jewel and one month plea.
Weeping Rama clasps Sita crest jewel to his heart, recalls its wedding history and begs Hanuman to repeat her every word.
Hanuman retells Sita crow and Brahma reed token, her plea why Rama spares Ravana, his comfort, and her tearful jewel and welfare messages.
Sita doubts sea crossing and craves glorious rescue by hosts, Hanuman vows leaping hosts will soon crown Rama with her in Ayodhya.
Rama praises Hanuman for impossible ocean leap and Lanka entry, embraces him as sole reward, then despairs over crossing the sea with monkeys.
Sugriva rebukes grieving Rama like a common man, promises to leap the ocean and storm Lanka, and urges him to trade grief for battle anger.
Rama asks Hanuman for Lanka defenses and troop strength, and Hanuman details gates, moats, engines, vast garrisons and urges an immediate auspicious march.
Rama orders an auspicious southward march with Nila vanguard, leads the roaring monkey host past Sahya Malaya, and camps to plan the ocean crossing.
Camped by the sea, Rama tells Lakshmana his grief grows daily, burns with love-fire for captive Sita, and longs to kill Ravana and embrace her.
Shamed by Hanuman burning Lanka, Ravana summons his rakshasas, defines best middle worst men and counsels, and seeks advice against approaching Rama.
Ravana counselors dismiss despair, recall his conquests over Kubera, Yakshas, Nagas, Danavas, Varuna sons and Yama, and promise he will kill Rama.
Prahasta, Durmukha, Vajradamshtra, Nikumbha and Vajrahanu each boast they alone will wipe out monkeys and kill Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva.
Armed champions vow to kill Rama, but Vibhishana restrains them, warns against scorning Hanuman feat, and urges returning Sita before arrows shatter Lanka.
Ravana calls kinsman Vibhishana a foe for urging Sita return, and Vibhishana rises skyward with four followers, warning doom-seized kings reject friendly counsel.
Vibhishana seeks Rama refuge from sky while Sugriva suspects treachery and ministers debate testing him as Hanuman trusts his honest face
Rama vows to shelter surrendered Vibhishana, cites dove and Kandu verses on protecting suppliants, and grants fearlessness to all comers
Rama embraces surrendered Vibhishana and crowns him Lanka king, then accepts his counsel to seek ocean aid and lies waiting on shore
Ocean ignores Rama worship for three nights, so enraged Rama seizes his bow and lashes the waters with blazing arrows
Ocean rises to promise safe passage and names Nala, whose monkey host builds a hundred-league bridge and crosses to Lanka shore
Ravana sends disguised Shuka and Sarana to count the army, but Rama frees the captured spies and threatens Lanka ruin by tomorrow
Defiant Ravana views the boundless monkey host from his palace and has Sarana name its roaring chiefs Nila, Angada, Kumuda and others
Sarana continues naming fearless chiefs Dhumra, Jambavan, Kesari, Shatabali and countless Vindhya hosts eager to crush Lanka
Shuka names peerless Mainda, Dvivida, lone Lanka-crusher Hanuman, death-wrathful Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and garlanded Sugriva
Ravana spares praising Shuka and Sarana, then sends fresh spies who are seized by Vibhishana, mauled by monkeys and report Suvela camp
Shardula reports Rama camped on Suvela after Rama spares his life, lists monkey chiefs, and Ravana refuses to return Sita.
Ravana has Vidyujjihva craft a false head of Rama and tells Sita her husband and monkey army fell in a night slaughter.
Sita mourns over the false head of Rama and begs to join him in death before Ravana leaves for war counsel.
Sarama exposes the severed head as sorcery, shows Sita Rama camped alive, and foretells his victory over Ravana.
Sarama offers to bear a message to Rama, learns Ravana rejects pleas to return Sita, and predicts his death in battle.
Elder Malyavan urges Ravana to return Sita and make peace, citing dharma, wrathful sages, and dreadful portents over Lanka.
Ravana rejects Malyavan's plea for peace, vows never to yield Sita, and stations his captains at every gate of Lanka.
Vibhishana details Ravana's guards at every gate, and Rama assigns his captains to storm each entrance.
Rama leads the monkey host up Mount Suvela, views demon lined Lanka, and camps beneath the full moon.
Waking on Suvela, the monkeys roam Lanka groves while Rama beholds her walled palaces crowning Trikuta peak.
Rama blockades Lanka on all sides and sends Angada to demand Sita return, but Ravana orders seizure and Angada shatters his palace tower.
Ravana sees countless monkeys blockading Lanka and sends his hosts out, sparking a bloody godlike clash on ramparts and gates.
Monkey and rakshasa champions fight duels around Lanka while Rama, Lakshmana and leaders crush Ravana's best fighters.
Night falls over Lanka as Rama slaughters rakshasa leaders, but Angada wrecks Indrajit's chariot and Indrajit vanishes to shoot unseen.
Invisible Indrajit binds Rama and Lakshmana with snake arrows, felling both bloodied and motionless while grieving monkeys surround them.
Indrajit proclaims Rama and Lakshmana slain and cheers Lanka, while Vibhishana steadies fearful Sugriva and rallies the monkey army.
Ravana flies grieving Sita over the battlefield in Pushpaka to show Rama and Lakshmana apparently slain, leaving her lamenting their death.
Sita mourns Rama and Lakshmana as dead and calls her auspicious marks false, till Trijata proves them alive and leads her back.
Rama revives to find Lakshmana seemingly dead, vows to die with him, and bids Sugriva lead the monkeys home across the sea.
Garuda swoops down to free Rama and Lakshmana from snake arrows and heal them, sending roaring monkeys storming back toward Lanka gates.
Ravana hears the freed Rama and Lakshmana roaring, and sends Dhumraksha with a vast host through the west gate toward Hanuman.
Hanuman smashes Dhumraksha chariot with a hurled rock and crushes his skull with a mountain peak after fierce tree stone slaughter.
Ravana sends unshakable Akampana with a vast host, whose dusty clash blinds both armies until monkey chiefs ravage the vanguard.
Hanuman withstands Akampana arrow storm, shatters his peak missiles, and fells him with an ashvakarna tree as demons flee.
Ravana inspects guarded Lanka and sends commander Prahasta through the east gate with a vast host past dire omens.
Nila duels commander Prahasta with trees and rocks, survives his mace stroke, and crushes his skull as demons flee.
Rama rides Hanuman into battle, wrecks Ravana chariot, cuts his crown, and spares his life after Lakshmana falls to the Shakti.
Humiliated Ravana orders Kumbhakarna woken with meats wines and war din, and the waking giant vows to devour the monkey host.
Vibhishana recounts Kumbhakarna cursed six month slumber for devouring beings, and Nila arrays the monkeys with rocks at the gates.
Kumbhakarna enters Ravana palace in splendor and Ravana pleads for rescue as Rama with Sugriva ravages Lanka and slays its chiefs.
Laughing Kumbhakarna reproaches Ravana for thoughtless action, suffers angry rebuke for preaching, then promises to kill Rama with Lakshmana and feast on the monkey chiefs.
Mahodara rebukes Kumbhakarna as raw and boastful, defends Ravana knowledge of policy, then urges five warriors to feign bloody return and proclaim Rama devoured to win Sita without battle.

Kumbhakarna silences Mahodara as cowardly counselor, takes his shining iron spear with Ravana honors, then marches from Lanka with his army swelling mountainlike and scattering monkeys despite dire omens.
Angada halts the fleeing monkeys with shame and duty, leads a tree and rock assault that cannot move Kumbhakarna, then rallies the scattering chiefs to return to battle.
The rallied monkeys assault Kumbhakarna and are crushed, Sugriva duels and is carried toward Lanka before biting free, then Lakshmana and Rama strike off his arms and head amid gods rejoicing.
Hearing of Kumbhakarna's death, Ravana faints and laments his lost right arm, then recalls rejecting virtuous Vibhishana and blames his own deed for the sorrow.
Trishiras rebukes Ravana's grief and marches with Devantaka Narantaka Atikaya and Mahodara Mahaparshva, then Narantaka ravages the host till Sugriva sends Angada who crushes his chest with a fist.
Devantaka Mahodara and Trishiras jointly assault Angada, then Hanuman crushes Devantaka, Nila fells Mahodara with elephant, Hanuman beheads Trishiras, and Rishabha slays Mahaparshva.

Atikaya routs the monkey chiefs and challenges Rama, then duels Lakshmana through Agneya Saura Aisika Aindra Yamya and Vayavya darts till Vayu reveals his charmed armor and Lakshmana beheads him with the Brahma weapon.
Indrajit vows to lay Rama lifeless, worships fire at Nikumbhila for Brahma weapons and invisibility, then rains shafts from the sky felling monkeys and Rama with Lakshmana before reentering Lanka.
Vibhishana rallies despairing monkeys and Jambavan sends Hanuman to fetch healing herbs that revive Rama Lakshmana and fallen hosts.
Sugriva orders torch bearing monkeys to burn Lanka while Ravana looses Kumbha and Nikumbha and night battle rages.
Angada fells Kampana and Sugriva trades praise and vajra fists to crush Kumbha as earth shakes.
Hanuman withstands Nikumbha iron parigha and tears off his head as battle between Rama and demon hosts rages.
Ravana blazing over Kumbha and Nikumbha deaths sends Khara son Makaraksha who boasts of killing Rama past dire omens.
Rama answers Makaraksha duel challenge, shatters his bow chariot and spear, then fells him with a fire weapon.
Indrajit kindles war fire, mounts unseen chariot, and rains unseen shafts that pierce Rama Lakshmana while Rama forbids indiscriminate Brahma weapon.
Indrajit conjures illusory Sita on his chariot and swords her before grieving Hanuman to break monkey resolve.
Hanuman rallies fleeing monkeys, hurls a vain rock at Indrajit, then withdraws to report Sita death as Indrajit kindles Nikumbhila fire.
Hanuman reports Sita slaughter and Rama swoons while Lakshmana denounces useless dharma and vows to fell Lanka.
Vibhishana exposes Sita slaughter as Indrajit illusion and urges Rama to send Lakshmana before Nikumbhila rite ends.
Rama orders Lakshmana with monkey bears and Vibhishana to reach Nikumbhila and slay Indrajit before his rite.
Lakshmana breaks the demon screen while Hanuman batters hosts and Vibhishana marks out Indrajit for slaughter.
Vibhishana shows Lakshmana the dark Nyagrodha shrine and rebukes traitor taunts by defending his righteous desertion of Ravana.
Boastful Indrajit and fearless Lakshmana trade taunts and arrow storms in a matched duel of man lion and demon lion.
Lakshmana shatters Indrajit armor and both bloodied champions hurl endless weapons until Vibhishana relieves Lakshmana fatigue.
Vibhishana rallies monkeys past slain chiefs while Lakshmana beheads Indrajit driver and crushes his horses and chariot.
Lakshmana swears by Rama truth and looses the all conquering Indra shaft that severs helmeted Indrajit head.
Bloodied Lakshmana reports Indrajit death while Rama embraces him and Sushena herb heals him and wounded monkeys.
Grief maddened Ravana laments Indrajit rushes sword in hand to murder Sita, then yields to Suparshva and returns.
Rama alone annihilates Ravana vast host with Gandharva weapon while deluded demons slay each other, and fleeing survivors reach Lanka.
Lanka widows blame Shurpanakha lust and Ravana pride for ruin, recall Rama killings, and foresee Sita destroying rakshasas.
Ravana ignores death omens, marches with three generals and vast arms, and slaughters scattering monkey hosts.
Sugriva rallies fleeing monkeys, duels Virupaksha through elephant tree sword and fist, and crushes his temple dead.
Sugriva duels Mahodara through rock arrows mace musala and swords, beheading him and routing his troops.
Angada rallies arrow shattered monkeys, trades parigha axe and blows with Mahaparshva, and bursts his heart dead.
Ravana burns monkey ranks with darkness weapon, then trades arrow floods and serpent arrows with Rama, whose fire weapon dissolves them.
Ravana hurls Maya spear through Lakshmana chest, grieving Rama vows single combat, and drives fleeing Ravana off.
Sushena finds Lakshmana alive, Hanuman fetches healing mountain peak, and revived Lakshmana urges Rama to keep his vow.
Indra sends Matali with his chariot for grounded Rama, who mounts it and counters serpent arrows with eagles.
Ravana hurls a blazing pike at Rama, Rama shatters it with Indra's javelin, then wounds Ravana's horses and bloodies his whole body.
Rama mocks Ravana as a cowardly wife thief, showers him with arrows, and leaves him dazed till his driver bears him from battle.
Ravana rebukes his driver for withdrawing, hears his plea of weary horses and ill omens, then rewards him and rushes back toward Rama.
Rama meets Ravana's charging chariot with Matali's circling drive while dire omens doom Ravana and bright omens promise Rama victory.
Rama fells Ravana's banner after Ravana misses his, then both loose endless arrow floods and slay each other's horses.
Rama beheads Ravana a hundred times without killing him, then wonders why his once deadly arrows prove dull while battle rages night and day.
Reminded by Matali, Rama consecrates Brahma's unfailing arrow, pierces Ravana's heart, and watches gods rain flowers as monkeys rout the leaderless rakshasas.
Ravana's widows rush to the battlefield, collapse upon his corpse, and lament that scorning Vibhishana's counsel and keeping Sita doomed them all to fate.
Mandodari mourns Ravana as undone by lust for Sita, then Rama overrules Vibhishana's refusal and has him cremate his brother.
After Matali departs heavenward, Rama crowns loyal Vibhishana in Lanka and sends Hanuman to tell Sita of his safety and Ravana's death.
Hanuman enters Lanka to tell Sita of Rama victory, receives her grateful speechless joy, offers to slay tormenting rakshasis, and hears her plea for forgiveness capped by an old verse on compassion.
Hanuman tells Rama that Sita longs to see him, Rama orders adorned Sita brought in state, halts the clearing of his own crowds declaring conduct veils women, and receives shy weeping Sita with joy.

Before monkeys and rakshasas Rama boasts his victory and lineage honour, renounces Ravana-touched Sita as a lamp to sore eyes, and bids her go freely to Lakshmana Bharata Sugriva or Vibhishana while she trembles weeping.

Pierced by harsh public rejection Sita protests her chaste heart and helpless limbs, reproaches Rama for ignoring her birth devotion and childhood hand, and enters fire after Lakshmana builds a pyre amid wailing crowds.

As Sita falls the guardians Kubera Yama Indra Varuna Shiva and Brahma arrive to rebuke Rama indifference, hear him claim humanity, and praise him as Narayana Vishnu bearing worlds who entered flesh to slay Ravana.

Fire rises with unburnt adorned Sita proving her word mind and eye chastity, commands Rama to take her back, and Rama explains his public ordeal as needed purification before the worlds before joyful reunion.

Shiva bids Rama console kin regain Ayodhya and ascend after horse rite, Dasharatha embraces Rama and Lakshmana from his vimana recalling sorrow and Kaikeyi words, and blesses Lakshmana and Sita before returning to Indra world.

After Dasharatha departs Indra grants Rama boon to revive fallen monkeys woundless with out-of-season fruits roots and clear rivers, and the gods bid him go console Sita meet Bharata and consecrate himself in Ayodhya.

Resting overnight Rama defers bath and ornaments until seeing Bharata, declines Vibhishana feast to hasten to Ayodhya by the hard road, and accepts Kubera Pushpaka vimana while its golden jewelled splendour is detailed.

Rama has Vibhishana honour striving monkeys with jewels, boards Pushpaka with bashful Sita and Lakshmana, permits allies to leave, and at their wish to witness consecration takes Sugriva host and Vibhishana aboard as the vimana rises.
Rama shows Sita Lanka battlefield, ocean bridge, Kishkindha and forest sites from Pushpaka, then vanaras behold gleaming Ayodhya.
Bharadvaja welcomes Rama home, recounts his forest war triumphs by tapas, and ripens fruit honey trees along Ayodhya road.
Rama sends Hanuman to Ayodhya to test Bharata intent, and Hanuman finds matted Bharata ruling from padukas in Nandigrama.
Hanuman retells Rama exile, Sita search, Lanka war and Pushpaka return to Bharata, promising Rama arrival tomorrow.
Bharata adorns the Nandigrama road, greets Rama in Pushpaka with mothers and citizens, returns padukas and kingdom, then dismisses vimana.
Bharata restores the kingdom, Rama bathes, enters Ayodhya, crowns with Sita amid gods, rewards allies, and rules a blameless ten-thousand-year realm.
Sages congratulate Rama on killing Ravana and kin, marvel most at Indrajit slaying, and surprised Rama asks for Indrajit power boon and Indra tale.
Agastya traces Ravana clan to Pulastya, whose curse on sporting maidens weds him to Trinabindu daughter and fathers Vishrava.
Bharadvaja weds daughter to Vishrava, whose son Vaishravana wins fourth guardianship wealth lordship and Pushpaka from Brahma and settles empty Lanka.
Agastya traces first rakshasas and yakshas to Brahma word, then Heti line to abandoned Sukesha, whom Shiva makes ageless and grants sky city.
Sukesha sons Malyavan Sumali Mali win invincibility from Brahma through penance, occupy Vishvakarman-built Lanka, wed Narmada daughters and torment gods.
Gods beg Shiva then Vishnu against boon-proud Malyavan kin, Vishnu promises their death, and rakshasa host marches to heaven scorning dire omens.
Vishnu scatters the rakshasa host with Sharnga arrows and Panchajanya blast, then beheads charging Mali with his discus and routs survivors toward Lanka.
Malyavan duels Vishnu with spear and fist, Garuda sweeps him away, and survivors quit Lanka for Patala, for only Narayana, now Rama, can slay them.
Sumali gives Kaikasi to Vishrava at dread hour, she bears ten-headed Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and righteous Vibhishana, and spurs Ravana to vow penance matching Vaishravana.
Ravana offers nine heads into fire and wins immunity with restored heads, Vibhishana wins steadfast dharma and immortality, and tricked Kumbhakarna asks years of sleep.
Sumali urges boon-armed Ravana to reclaim Lanka, Prahasta wins his assent, Kubera yields the city on Vishravas advice and Ravana enters consecrated.
Ravana gives Shurpanakha to Vidyujjihva, weds Maya daughter Mandodari, settles his brothers marriages, and fathers thunder-voiced Meghanada.
Kumbhakarna sinks into long sleep in his vast palace while Ravana ravages gardens, slays Kubera envoy rejecting counsel, and marches for triple-world conquest.
Ravana leads six ministers to Kailasa, crushes the roused Yaksha host with mace and ministers, and smashes the gate guardian to seize the portal.
Kubera confronts Ravana with moral rebuke, exchanges mace blows and divine missiles, falls to maya-aided mace stroke, and loses Pushpaka to victorious Ravana.
Pushpaka halts at Shiva mountain, Nandi curses monkey-born ruin for Ravana mockery, Shiva pins his lifting arms and names roaring Ravana.
Ravana propositions ascetic Vedavati in Himalayan forest, she rejects Vishnu-scorn and violation, then enters fire vowing rebirth as his destroyer Sita.
Ravana challenges sacrificing Marutta barred from battle, Shuka proclaims him victor after he devours sages, and gods reward sheltering beasts with boons.
Ravana forces Dushyanta and other kings to yield, kills resisting Ayodhya king Anaranya, who dying curses an Ikshvaku-born slayer of Ravana.
Narada meets conquering Ravana, turns him from hapless mortals toward Yama city, then meditates and follows curious to Yama abode.
Narada warns Yama of Ravana, who storms the realm of death, frees punished souls, routs guards with Pashupata fire and roars triumphantly.
Yama battles Ravana for seven nights, raises the fatal Time staff, yields to Brahma bidding, vanishes, while Ravana proclaims victory and marches out.
Ravana befriends the Nivatakavachas through Brahma, slays Kalakeya Daityas, routs Varuna sons in sky battle and leaves upon learning Varuna is absent.
Ravana seizes wailing maidens for Pushpaka, earns chaste curse of death through woman, consoles widowed Shurpanakha and grants Khara Dandaka with fourteen thousand rakshasas.
Ravana meets sacrificer Meghanada laden with Shiva boons, learns Madhu abducted Kumbhinasi, marches to Madhupura, spares Madhu for alliance and camps toward heaven.
Lustful Ravana seizes Rambha bound for Nalakubara, assaults her despite plea as daughter-in-law, and suffers Nalakubara curse of seven-split head for future unwilling assault.
Terrified Indra begs Vishnu, who vows future death of Ravana, while gods battle rakshasas until Vasu Savitra crushes Sumali and scatters nightstalkers.
Meghanada routs gods and drives Jayanta away, Puloma rescues Jayanta to ocean, Indra meets Ravana while gods shred rakshasa ranks into bloody river.
Outnumbered Ravana rages through darkness while Indra orders live capture, then invisible Meghanada with granted maya binds Indra and bears him home triumphant.
Brahma names Meghanada Indrajit, grants battle-rite invulnerability for freeing Indra, then tells shamed Indra his Ahalya sin caused capture and prescribes Vaishnava sacrifice.
Ravana finds Arjuna absent at Mahishmati, vaunts that sun wind and Narmada fear him, then bathes and worships Shiva with flowers.
Arjuna dams the Narmada sportingly, floods Ravana worship, routs his ministers, then stuns Ravana with a mace and binds him like Bali.
Pulastya hastens to Mahishmati, honors conquering Arjuna, secures Ravana release and fire-witnessed friendship, then Agastya warns Rama that stronger men always exist.
Ravana challenges Vali at Kishkindha, gets tucked under his armpit through four oceans during twilight rites, then begs fire-witnessed brotherhood.
Rama extols Hanuman ocean leap and Lanka burning, doubts his sparing Vali, and learns sages cursed him to forget his strength.
Brahma revives the thunderstruck child, gods shower him with immunity boons, and sages later curse him to forget his strength for years.
Rama embraces Pratardana and sends him to guarded Varanasi, then credits allied kings for Ravana death and grants them leave to depart.
Boastful kings head home with gifts for Rama, which Bharata delivers and Rama redistributes to Sugriva Vibhishana monkeys before joyful two-month feasting.
Rama sends Sugriva to thornless Kishkindha and Vibhishana to righteous Lanka, then grants Hanuman deathlessness while his story lasts and tearful hosts depart.
Pushpaka returns at Kubera command for Rama service, Rama worships and frees it, then Bharata hails golden age portents and Rama rejoices.
Rama feasts with pregnant Sita in the Ashoka grove, learns her longing for Ganga hermitages, and promises to send her there tomorrow.
Rama asks Bhadra for city gossip, hears citizens praise bridge and mock his reclaiming Ravana-held Sita, then dismisses his stricken friends.
Rama summons his three brothers through doorkeeper, shows his tear-stained eclipsed-moon face, and begs their counsel for his resolve.
Rama cites cruel city slander of pure Sita, chooses fame over love, and orders Lakshmana to abandon her at Valmiki hermitage.
Lakshmana bears delighted gift-laden Sita toward the Ganga past dark omens, halts by Gomati, and weeps on reaching its waters.
Lakshmana ferries Sita across the Ganga, confesses Rama abandons her guiltless for city slander, and commends her to Valmiki.
Sita falls swooning at abandonment, sends Rama counsel to win citizens by righteousness, and watches Lakshmana sail away weeping.
Valmiki greets wailing Sita with honied welcome, attests her sinlessness by penance sight, and entrusts her to kindly ascetic women.
Grieving Lakshmana laments fate-driven banishment to Sumantra, who bids him not grieve and recalls brahmins foretelling Rama sorrow and partings.
Sumantra recounts Durvasas telling Dasharatha of Rama long reign, horse sacrifices, future kin partings, and ascent to Brahmaloka, cheering Lakshmana.
Lakshmana returns to Ayodhya, finds Rama weeping, reports leaving Sita at Valmiki hermitage, and consoles grieving Rama with impermanence.
Over hundred Yamuna sages bearing tirtha water visit Rama, praise his devotion, and beg rescue from great fear.
Cyavana tells Rama how Shiva gave Madhu a spear that passed to cruel Lavana tormenting worlds and sages.
Rama vows to kill man-eating Lavana, Bharata volunteers, Shatrughna insists instead, and Rama appoints Shatrughna king of Madhu city.
Shatrughna accepts command, Rama consecrates him, gives unfailing Madhu-Kaitabha arrow, and explains how to face spearless Lavana.
Rama grants Shatrughna troops treasure and tactics to travel secretly, kill Lavana after summer, and Shatrughna departs after saluting mothers.
Shatrughna rests at Valmiki hermitage and hears how hunter-king Saudasa fed Vasishtha human flesh and bore a twelve-year curse.
That night Sita bears twin sons at Valmiki hermitage, Valmiki names them Kusha and Lava, and Shatrughna rejoices before marching west.
Cyavana warns Shatrughna that spear-armed Lavana burned mighty Mandhata with army, yet predicts certain victory over weaponless Lavana tomorrow.
Shatrughna waits armed at Madhu gate, Lavana returns with prey, mocks him, invokes Ravana, and Shatrughna denies him time to fetch spear.
Shatrughna battles Lavana, survives tree blows and faint, looses Vishnu's infallible arrow to pierce his chest and free the worlds from fear.
Gods grant victorious Shatrughna a boon, he founds beautiful Madhupuri on Yamuna, and rules prosperous fearless Shurasena after twelve years.
Shatrughna visits Ayodhya after twelve years, reports Lavana slain and Mathura settled, and stays five nights at Rama's loving command.
A grieving old brahmin brings his dead five-year-old son to Rama's gate and blames untimely death on the king's misrule.
Narada tells Rama that a shudra's forbidden tapas in his realm causes the boy's death and urges him to find the offender.
Rama preserves the boy's body in oil, boards Pushpaka with bow and sword, and finds a head-hanging ascetic in the southern lake region.
Shambuka confesses shudra tapas for bodily godhood, Rama beheads him to revive the boy, and Agastya hosts Rama with a divine gift.
Agastya tells Rama how he finds a lifeless Treta forest, a corpse-filled lake, and a heaven-dweller eating his own flesh.
King Shveta tells Agastya how stingy tapas wins heaven with hunger, Brahma sets self-flesh as food, and the jewel buys his release.
Rama asks why Shveta's forest lies lifeless, and Agastya begins Manu's charge, Ikshvaku's hundred sons, and wayward Danda's new kingdom.
King Danda rapes sage Bhargava daughter Araja in the forest despite her warning, then flees to Madhumanta while she awaits her father.
Bhargava curses King Danda to die in seven nights and his hundred-yojana realm to perish in dust rain, creating Dandakaranya.
Rama worships at evening, feasts with Agastya overnight, takes sage leave, and flies Pushpaka back to Ayodhya.
Rama proposes the Rajasuya sacrifice, but Bharata warns it would destroy royal lines and Rama abandons the plan.
Lakshmana urges the Ashvamedha instead and begins telling how tapas-powerful Vritra terrified Indra into seeking Vishnu aid.
Vishnu splits himself into Indra, thunderbolt and earth to slay Vritra, leaving Indra stained by brahmahatya until an Ashvamedha.
Gods cleanse sense-stripped Indra with the Ashvamedha, quartering brahmahatya in rivers, trees, women and brahmana-slayers.
Hunting King Ila enters Shiva grove where all males turn female, then wins alternate months as woman and man.
Woman-formed Ila roams the forest with her retinue, churns Budha lake, and the sage settles her followers as Kimpurushis.
Budha loves woman-formed Ila for a month, keeps man-restored Ila a year, and she bears Pururavas before yielding him.
Rama recounts how woman-turned Ila regained manhood through a Shiva horse sacrifice, then founded Pratishthana before attaining Brahmaloka.
Rama resolves on a horse sacrifice, wins priestly approval, and sends Bharata ahead while inviting monkeys, rakshasas, kings, and sages to Naimisha.
Rama releases the sacrificial horse under Lakshmana guard and hosts a year-long Naimisha rite where monkeys and rakshasas feed all beggars unstintingly.
Valmiki reaches Naimisha and instructs his two pupils to sing the whole Ramayana daily before Rama, priests, and townsfolk without greed.
Rama hears two boys sing twenty sargas of Valmiki Ramayana, offers gold they refuse, and learns the epic spans five hundred sargas.
Recognizing the singers as Sita sons, Rama asks Valmiki to let sinless Sita swear publicly tomorrow, and the assembly applauds his resolve.
Before a vast Naimisha assembly, Valmiki leads tearful Sita forward, declares her sinless, and swears her twin sons belong to Rama.
Rama owns Sita sons before the gods, and Sita swears sole devotion to Rama before Earth goddess takes her into Rasatala amid flowers.
Rama mourns vanished Sita, rules Ayodhya with a golden Sita image, sacrifices ten thousand years, and honors his dead mothers.
Yudhajit envoy Gargya brings gifts urging conquest of Gandharva land, so Rama sends Bharata with Taksha and Pushkala to seize and settle it.
Bharata crushes three crore Gandharvas with the Samvarta weapon, founds Takshashila and Pushkaravati for Taksha and Pushkara, and returns to please Rama.
Rama founds Angadiya and Chandrakanta for Lakshmana sons Angada and Chandraketu, crowns them, and enjoys ten thousand righteous years with brothers.
Time arrives disguised as an ascetic demanding secret counsel with Rama, and Rama posts Lakshmana at the door under pain of death.
Time reveals himself as Brahma messenger recalling Vishnu-born Rama to heaven after his fixed human lifespan, and Rama agrees to depart.
Durvasa threatens to curse Rama city and race unless seen at once, forcing Lakshmana to break guarded talk, and Rama feeds the fasting sage.
Lakshmana begs Rama to keep his vow by killing him, Vasishtha orders abandonment, and Rama renounces him to ascend bodily to heaven.
Rama vows to crown Bharata and follow Lakshmana, citizens vow to follow him, so he crowns Kusha and Lava instead.
Shatrughna hears messengers tell Lakshmana loss and Rama departure, crowns Subahu at Mathura and Shatrughati at Vaidisha, and hastens to follow Rama.
Rama leads the great departure with fire umbrella and Vedic forms while queens, brothers, townsfolk, monkeys and bears joyfully follow.
Brahma meets Rama at the Sarayu, Rama enters Vishnu glory with brothers, and bathing followers abandon bodies to ascend allotted heavens.
